skill.description: Guides AI agents through GitHub project management workflows for issue triage, sprint planning, milestone tracking, project board updates, and stakeholder reports.

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are Markdown formatting false positives, not Ruby shell execution. The audit confirms the shell command substitution in the release milestone example and flags broader workflow risks from remote packages, repository-local scripts, GitHub mutations, and external sync.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the package version, document its source, and require explicit user approval before running npx-based setup commands.
Document required scripts, verify their contents before execution, and avoid running scripts from untrusted workspaces.
Require a dry-run summary and user confirmation before changing labels, assignments, milestones, project fields, or releases.
Use least-privilege credentials, redact webhook secrets, and require approval before sending data to Jira, Slack, or other services.

remediation.issue: Shell command substitution in GitHub metadata
remediation.suggestion: Replace command substitution with a vetted file argument or explicit reviewed content to reduce accidental data disclosure.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Alpha Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to run npx claude-flow@alpha, which can download and execute a remote alpha package during project management setup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands explicitly invoke npx claude-flow@alpha. Remote package execution is a clear supply chain risk even when used for legitimate orchestration.

semantic_findings.title: Repository-Local Script Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflows instruct agents to run local scripts such as github-webhook.sh, github-api.sh, project-api.sh, and analytics scripts that are not included in this skill package.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple instructions call bash scripts under scripts/. Because the package does not include those scripts, execution depends on workspace-local code that may be untrusted.

semantic_findings.title: Automated GitHub State Changes
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs automation to label issues, set project fields, assign users, set milestones, and create releases, which can modify repository state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited workflow steps explicitly perform GitHub mutations. The behavior is intended, but unsafe if broad credentials run without user confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: External Synchronization and Webhook Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes bidirectional Jira synchronization and Slack webhook posting, which can disclose issue metadata and expose webhook destinations if misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands name Jira sync and Slack webhook output directly. These are legitimate integrations, but they move project data outside GitHub.

content.user_title: Manage GitHub Projects With AI Workflows
content.value_statement: Teams lose time keeping issues, milestones, and project boards aligned. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured GitHub project management workflows.
actual_capabilities: Defines a star topology for coordinator, planner, issue tracker, and board sync agents.
Guides automated issue triage with classification, labels, assignments, and priority scoring.
Plans sprints with capacity checks, backlog review, milestone creation, and sprint board setup.
Tracks milestones, release readiness, project risks, and stakeholder status reports.
Documents GitHub Projects v2 custom field automation and analytics workflows.
limitations: Requires configured GitHub access, MCP tools, and local automation scripts.
Does not include the referenced shell scripts or reference templates.
Can change GitHub issues, milestones, releases, and project boards when executed.
External sync workflows need user approval and destination-specific credentials.

use_cases.title: Run Sprint Planning
use_cases.description: Prepare capacity, review backlog priority, create milestones, and initialize a sprint board.

use_cases.title: Triage Repository Issues
use_cases.description: Classify new issues, apply labels, assign owners, detect duplicates, and add items to a project board.

use_cases.title: Track Release Milestones
use_cases.description: Monitor milestone progress, identify delivery risks, prepare readiness checks, and generate stakeholder updates.

prompt_templates.title: Begin Issue Triage
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to triage new issues in my repository. Classify each issue, suggest labels, and ask before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Sprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan the next two-week sprint. Review team capacity, prioritize the backlog, and propose a sprint milestone.

prompt_templates.title: Sync A Project Board
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit my GitHub Projects v2 board. Identify stale items, missing fields, blocked work, and recommended updates.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate A Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to track release readiness. Review milestone health, identify risks, prepare stakeholder status, and request approval before actions.

output_examples.input: Triage five new issues for a web app repository.
output: Issue classification with type, severity, component, and duplicate risk.
Recommended labels, owner, priority, and milestone for each issue.
A list of GitHub changes that need user approval before execution.

output_examples.input: Prepare Sprint 42 for the platform team.
output: Sprint capacity summary with unavailable time and planning buffer.
Prioritized sprint candidate list grouped by theme and dependency.
Milestone and project board update plan with approval checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Create a release health update for version 2.0.
output: Milestone progress summary with completed, blocked, and at-risk work.
Release readiness checklist and unresolved dependency list.
Stakeholder update draft with risks, next actions, and target dates.

best_practices: Review planned GitHub changes before allowing the agent to apply them.
Use least-privilege GitHub tokens and scoped credentials for external systems.
Keep label taxonomy, team ownership, and sprint templates current.
anti_patterns: Do not run repository-local scripts from untrusted projects without review.
Do not let automation close, assign, or release work without human approval.
Do not send project data to Slack, Jira, or other tools without consent.

faq.question: Does this skill directly connect to GitHub?
faq.answer: It provides workflows and command guidance. Actual access depends on configured GitHub tools, tokens, and scripts.

faq.question: Can it manage GitHub Projects v2 boards?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes workflows for custom fields, board status, sprint views, and Projects v2 synchronization.

faq.question: Does it include the referenced scripts?
faq.answer: No. The skill references local scripts and templates that must exist in the user workspace.

faq.question: Is it suitable for small teams?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflows cover small teams, larger teams, kanban boards, sprints, and release milestones.

faq.question: Should commands run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Commands that change GitHub or send data to external tools should require user confirmation.

faq.question: What tools work with this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the required project tools are available.
